fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Nighttime conspicuity of a HAWK display against background clutter is a recognized, site-specific safety issue in the FHWA Tucson case study lineage, directly bearing on drivers' stop decisions while pedestrians cross the arterial.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim (driver confusion from competing night-time background elements at Speedway Blvd/Rook Ave) is supported by a verbatim quoted passage in EV-US-001, exceeding registry-id-only citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern under FHWA RSA semantics with no compliance claim conflated in, and normative_basis_note appropriately left null.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Retroreflective border/backplate treatment is specific, located, actionable at final design stage, and a standard FHWA countermeasure that directly targets the stated conspicuity problem.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly identified as the exposed road users, with the driver-confusion-to-pedestrian-risk link acknowledged in the scenario text.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance timing adequacy for slower walkers at the corridor's highest pedestrian-collision HAWK sites is a real, design-stage-addressable safety issue, not vacuous.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is backed by a verbatim quoted passage from EV-US-016 ('The pedestrian clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians') plus the recorded TABLE A.10 Issue 2 site linkage; no invented content.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern asking to verify assumed walking speeds under FHWA RSA semantics, kept categorically distinct from any MUTCD compliance assertion.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Reprogramming clearance intervals at all six named sites with a reduced assumed walking speed is specific, actionable, and viable at final design stage; not a null recommendation.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are the explicit focus: pedestrians and elderly pedestrians are named road users and the entire concern addresses their clearance exposure, so fully considered.
